tagline: North from a refinery town over the Seminoe Mountains.
intro: North from Sinclair, County Road 351 leaves I-80 for pronghorn-grazed prairie and stark desert, then climbs the rugged Seminoe Mountains. Seminoe, Pathfinder and Alcova reservoirs break up the dry country, and the road crosses the Miracle Mile of the North Platte on its way to Alcova.
The first mining claim in these mountains was registered in 1868 by three miners. None of them lived to work it. Gold found later set off a rush in 1871, and the first mining period was over by 1874.

moments.title: Sinclair
moments.text: Built in 1924 and 1925 as Parco, a Spanish Colonial Revival company town, its original refinery, just east of town, is still in use.

moments.title: Seminoe Mountains
moments.text: Just north of Seminoe State Park the road turns very steep and stays that way through the mountains to the Miracle Mile.

moments.title: Miracle Mile
moments.text: The backway crosses this stretch of the North Platte, a blue-ribbon trout fishery.

practical: Paved and gravel, generally passable from May to November, with no services or gas until Alcova; the steep stretch from north of Seminoe State Park to the Miracle Mile is not recommended for motor homes or vehicles pulling trailers.
